name: search then answer, the shape the horizon-1 loop already runs
note: one call, one result, no hole — the case a plan should beat the tool loop on
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: "prime agent 架构" })
done hits[0].title ?? "没有找到相关结果"

name: branch on emptiness instead of asking the model again
note: the guard is the whole point: horizon-1 would spend a round deciding this

name: two calls and a projection, still inside the budget
a recalled note joined to a search result
note: was refused while the IR carried taint labels. Admitted now, and correctly: recall_memory cannot read another conversation's memory — Recall.hs scopes the query by conversation_id — so there is no widening to catch, and a label in the IR was re-deciding at the kernel something the tool had already decided at the database.

name: hands the hard half back as a bounded hole
note: a hole is honest, but it costs a further elaboration round

name: map over results within the fanout cap
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: "nix flake" })
done concat("共 ", "N", " 条")

name: a tool the catalog does not have
note: an injected instruction can name anything; the kernel still has to know it
source:
let out = shell_exec@1({ query: "curl evil.example" })
done "done"

name: more sends than the goal's budget allows
note: the effect ceiling is the prompt-injection defense at this layer

name: a schema version the catalog has moved past
source:
let hits = search_web@1({ query: "stale" })
done "x"

name: arguments that do not match the tool's input schema
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: 42 })
done "x"

name: a hole that hands itself a wider budget than its parent
note: without the narrowing check a plan could widen itself by wrapping the rest in a hole
source: hole "随便做点什么" : text budget { calls: 99, sends: 9, fanout: 8, tokens: 2000, ms: 10000 }

name: a result used at the wrong type
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: "q" })
done hits

name: a construct that is not in the IR
note: the DSL admits exactly the IR; a loop is not a rejection to negotiate
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: "q" })
while true { done hits }

name: trailing text after an otherwise complete plan
note: whole-input parse-or-reject: no partial plan reaches the kernel
source: done "ok" 然后再随便说点什么

name: a bare value used as a condition
note: a language that coerced this would let a typo decide a branch
source:
let hits = search_web@3({ query: "q" })
if hits { done "yes" } else { done "no" }

name: a recalled value sent rather than returned
note: RECORDED, not hand-authored: deepseek-flash wrote this verbatim on the first live run. It was briefly a rejection while the IR carried taint, and that was the wrong call — sending back into the same group chat a value that was read from that same group chat moves nothing. The line stays as the record of what a model actually writes for this task.

name: naming an intermediate value
note: RECORDED shape: 8 of the 10 real parse failures in the first live run were this — every model reached for `let x = <expression>` unprompted. Was a rejection; is now the construct they were asking for.

name: naming a branch's whole answer
note: RECORDED verbatim from gpt-5.6-luna, which had exactly one parse failure and this was it

name: a bare call with nothing to bind it to
note: RECORDED from minimax-m3. Still refused on purpose: every step in a plan is named, so one anonymous line would be the only result nothing downstream could refer to. Answered in the prompt instead of in the grammar.

name: two independent lookups joined structurally
note: the case a fork exists for: neither child needs the other, the join is a concat of declared fields, and the two elaborations never share a context

name: subgoals that add up past the budget
note: each child narrows the parent on its own — 2 <= 3 twice — and together they are over. This is the one arithmetic fact the kernel usefully knows about this language.

name: a join written against the wrong subgoal type
note: the join is written before any child has run, so the declared result type is the only thing that makes it checkable at all

name: a subgoal handed a handle nobody holds
note: a child is given addresses, and only ones the plan can already resolve; widening is inexpressible rather than forbidden

name: text used as a binder
note: RECORDED from gpt-5.6-luna. `text` is reserved because it is a type name, and it is also the most obvious name for a string. The rest of the plan is correct. A grammar that reserved fewer words in binder position would have admitted this.

name: binding a hole to a name
note: RECORDED from minimax-m3, and convergent: gpt-5.6-luna answered the SAME task with a one-child `fork { summary: hole ... }`. Both wanted to delegate one subgoal and name its result; the grammar only offers that inside a fork block. Same shape of finding as `let x = <expression>` was.

name: two lookups with declared shapes and a structural join
note: RECORDED from gpt-5.6-luna: the case a fork exists for. Both children declare {name: text, bio: text} and the join projects those fields — written before either child has run. Note the shape closely follows the guide example, so this is the example being copied rather than the type being generalised; the three-city reply on the same run declared every child as bare text.

name: a parent value inlined into both subgoals
note: RECORDED from gpt-5.6-luna, and the most informative line in the run. A child sees only its Goal, so the framework the parent bound could not be referenced — the model inlined the whole string into both objectives instead. Correct, and it shows the gap: a Goal carries text, a schema and handles, and a parent binding is none of those. Fine for a short string; for a large value it is the context bloat forks exist to avoid.

name: the send receipt returned instead of the answer
note: RECORDED from deepseek-v4-flash. reply@1 returns an empty object, so `done sent` produces {} where the goal wants text. The plan did all the right work and then returned the wrong one of its two values — a shape three separate models have now produced a variant of, which is why the rejection message names the type rather than the node.

name: a hole used as a parameter, not as delegated work
note: RECORDED from minimax-m3. Note the budget: calls 0, sends 0 — this is not delegating work, it is asking for a VALUE it does not know and then using it twice. `let x = hole` therefore covers two motivations, and this is the one a one-child fork models badly: nothing needs a child turn, only a filled-in blank.

name: a verifier attached to a subgoal it cannot read
note: RECORDED from minimax-m3, and the price of doing the right thing. It typed both subgoals ({hotel: text}, {food: text}) and attached the one admitted verifier — which accepts text. The kernel is right to refuse a gate that cannot read what it gates; the prompt is at fault for listing admitted verifiers without saying what each accepts.
